main_statement.latex: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial $f\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\Q^n$.
main_statement.paraphrase: H10 over Q is undecidable; more precisely H10(Z) <=_T H10(Q), so H10(Q) has Turing degree 0' (Cor 07-consequences.tex:8-23), also for degree <= 4 inputs.
main_statement.how_mazur_is_avoided: No Diophantine definition or Diophantine model of Z is constructed (07-consequences.tex:105-107). The reduction is a Turing reduction that uses negative oracle answers: f has no integer zero iff some finite existential test is unsolvable over Q. Mazur's conjecture (and Cornelissen-Zahidi's extension) obstruct only positive-existential definitions/models, so the paper neither disproves nor depends on Mazur's conjecture; the intro says this (01-introduction.tex:76-87). Phi is a Diophantine set containing Z but dense, which is compatible with Mazur.
main_statement.route_classification: NOT Koenigsmann/Poonen definitions, NOT a Diophantine model, NOT Shlapentokh/Poonen rank-stability for rings. Route = model theory (Skolem/Herbrand tests + compactness) + elliptic indices on a rank-one curve over Q(sqrt2) (Poonen-2002-style local reading) + a new radical-controlled height estimate (von Kaenel modular method on a Shimura curve) + GTZ prime patterns + a parity Diophantine predicate needing a 2-converse.

ms2_statement.paraphrase: E/Q with E(Q)[2]!=0 and 2^inf-Selmer corank s_2 in {0,1}: analytic rank = rank = s_2 and Sha finite.

items.name: Finite rational tests: Herbrand-style ground-instance tests decided by the H10(Q) oracle
items.statement: For nonconstant f, an effective sequence of finite tests, each a finite conjunction of ground instances of the Skolemized theory T+{f(a)=0}+Phi, translated into finitely many rational-solvability queries; f has an integer zero iff every test succeeds. Run integer search and test-failure search in parallel.

cited_or_new.cue: we construct an effectively generated sequence of finite tests

load_bearing_guess.reason: This is the global strategy that sidesteps Mazur's obstruction: it uses NEGATIVE oracle answers (a failing existential test), so no Diophantine definition or model of Z is produced (07-consequences.tex:100-107).

analytic_check.note: The goal mentions only an algorithm and rational zeros; neither Skolem ground terms nor compactness occur in it. But the logical scaffold (Skolemization, Herbrand ground instances, compactness) is textbook logic/automated reasoning (Herbrand 1930, Gilmore 1960, Davis-Putnam 1960).

provisional_N.grade: N2 (as a logic device N0 transfer; the bridge to H10(Q) looks new)
provisional_N.justification: Scaffold = Herbrand/Gilmore/compactness (N0 transfer from logic/automated reasoning). Using it to get H10(Z) <=_T H10(Q) without a Diophantine model: no precedent found in quick search (Yuyama's notes, snippet only, say the only known undecidability method goes through Diophantine models).

proof_architecture.claim: Fix a rank-one curve E over F=Q(sqrt2) (I05, I06) and its conjugate; formal-log comparisons (I10) read index ratios locally.
Local comparison (I11): with h, j_0 independent of a, two tests (main curve, conjugate curve) give a~ = eta(a) mod q^K without multiplicativity of eta.
Five-point height estimate (I12): heights of P^1-points bounded polynomially in odd-contact radical, via Shimura curve disc 210 and von Kaenel's modular height method (needs OAI Fontaine-Mazur at 2).
Recursive theory T (I15): representation axiom writes every ring element as three slopes whose contact values are tested primes with local witnesses; integer model from GTZ prime patterns (I14, I44).
Pole-parity formula Phi (I17): positive existential, true on Z (needs MS2 2-converse + Cassels-Tate), forces even poles outside S_1.
Finite tests (I04, I18): ground instances of Skolemized T+f(a)=0+Phi; each finite part is an H10(Q) query; failure is sound.
If all tests succeed, compactness (I19) gives R in *Q; coarsening (I20) maps odd-contact ambient primes to tested branches; index congruences (I21).

Height squeeze (I22): delta=f(eta(a)) is divisible by M^K for every slope of every ring element, so h(A~)<<B for all A; canonical height of eta(a_j)P is ~B^2, so B is standard and a is an integer root.
Parallel search gives H10(Z) <=_T H10(Q); DPRM finishes; Turing degree 0' and degree-4 normal form (I51).

2-converse: cyclotomic (Kato) and ring-class (Heegner/Kolyvagin) determinant families over binary cubes of quadratic twists; Chevalley-Warning transfers bounds to the missing vertex; half-integral-weight coefficient tests turned into binary symbols; address lemma programs auxiliary prime networks so all nonzero vertices are units.

correctness_audit.verdict: Section 2 (logic and the height squeeze) checked line by line: no gap found. The arithmetic inputs are deep and two rest on unreviewed OAI manuscripts. Plausible but not trustworthy without expert review of MS2, family 010 and Section 4.
checked: Herbrand/Skolem tests: every axiom of T quantifies only over R, so it survives restriction to the term-generated subring (the reason Koenigsmann's universal definition could not be used this way).
Local comparison: (ii) gives v_q(eta((h-4)a))>=K, hence V_a=4 eta(a), V_1=4 mod q^K, V_1 a unit (q odd), then truncated-log assertion applies.
Odd-contact step: one of the five contact valuations equals t=min(v(u),v(v)) at q not in S_K, another differs by an odd amount, so some listed value has odd valuation and its r has odd v_q.
Coarsening: J-values even by Phi applied to b and ab; odd v_q(r) is positive mod J; centre is one of the two branch ideals since R_F/rR_F = (R/rR)^2.
Height squeeze: M_K^K | delta, |delta| <= C B^D, K >= cD, so slope heights << B; sum of three slopes; x(T_a) from three ring elements; canonical height gives B^2 << B.
Arithmetic spot checks: N(75-53sqrt2)=7; Q=(-dw, 2sqrt2 d^2) on E (python); disc-210 Shimura curve genus 5, e_3=e_4=0, Riemann-Hurwitz r=5; 2-part of gcd(d1,d2) is 4 for r=1 mod 8.
residual_concerns: MS2 (2-converse at p=2 for all reduction types, with no residual irreducibility) is a frontier-level claim, read only at architecture level here (cyclotomic section read in full). If MS2 fails, Phi is unproved on Z and the reduction's soundness fails (an integer zero might fail a test).

Family 010 (odd regular Fontaine-Mazur at 2 with no residual hypothesis) would itself be a major theorem. My assessment, not verified: it is probably avoidable here because the representations come from Q-building blocks, which are modular by Ribet/Pyle plus Khare-Wintenberger.
Section 4 combines many quantitative inputs (Gaudron-Remond with dimension growing like M^C, Javanpeykar, Pazuki); exponent bookkeeping looked consistent but was not rederived.
Lemma hei:base-height constructs theta-null maps on covers; plausible, not fully checked.
The algorithm is non-uniform (constants exist but are not computed); fine for undecidability.
